sections.html:
In the Shenandoah Valley, Harrisonburg serves as the seat of Rockingham County while remaining an independent city with its own government. It spans 17.39 square miles at about 1,325 feet of elevation and had 51,814 residents in the 2020 census. It became a city in 1916, after a settlement that dates to 1779.

The ground is rolling upland, with local relief of 100 to 300 feet, and six watersheds cross it, the largest being Blacks Run with 8.67 miles of stream. Hillside drainage and creek corridors matter on some streets and not at all on others, so look at your own lot before a buyer's inspector does.

Locals once called the place Rocktown. It took its name from Thomas Harrison, who settled in the valley in 1737 and claimed more than 12,000 acres near where the Spotswood Trail met the main Native American road through the valley. He deeded 2.5 acres for a courthouse in 1779 and 50 more acres in 1780, and that land is now historic downtown.

Downtown has Gothic Revival churches, early twentieth century warehouses and a poultry shipping plant from 1908, and the blocks around them hold houses built across more than a century. Older homes often carry deferred maintenance, which is a common reason owners choose an as-is sale.

With James Madison University enrolling over 20,000 students and Eastern Mennonite University about 2,000, the housing market moves with the school calendar. Landlords near campus notice it most, since a lease ending mid-year can leave a unit vacant for months.

The city's economic development office can supply current figures on employers and growth if you want them.

Interstate 81 is the main north-south route through the valley and passes through Harrisonburg. U.S. 11, U.S. 33 and State Routes 42, 253 and 280 also serve the city. A house near an I-81 exit suits commuters and freight drivers, and it also sits close to traffic noise.

The city school division operates two high schools, Harrisonburg High School and Rocktown High School, plus Skyline Middle School and Thomas Harrison Middle School and six elementary schools. Zoning can change, so call the division about a specific address.

Four distinct seasons visit Harrisonburg, from hot, humid summers to cool or cold winters. The city is in USDA hardiness zone 6b, with average winter lows between minus 5 and 0 degrees Fahrenheit.

Cold of that kind is hard on pipes in unheated spaces, on roofs and on aging heating equipment. Inspectors usually open with the furnace and attic. Knowing the furnace's age ahead of time lets you answer on the spot and keeps the price from being reopened late.

sections.h2: Real estate tax: rate, due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The rate is $1.01 per $100 of assessed value for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and City Council votes on it every April. Two bills a year cover the two halves of the tax year, and a deadline on a weekend or holiday shifts to the next business day.

Billing periodDue dateIf paid late
July through DecemberDecember 510 percent penalty, $10 minimum; 10 percent annual interest from January 1
January through JuneJune 510 percent penalty, $10 minimum; 10 percent annual interest from July 1

The city's real estate tax page lists three ways to pay:

  • Online, with a service fee added at checkout.
  • In person, through the City Hall drop box at 409 S. Main St.
  • By mail to the Treasurer's Office, P.O. Box 1007, Harrisonburg, VA 22803-1007.

Elderly and disabled owners may qualify for tax relief, and a separate exemption exists for disabled military service members. Ask the Commissioner of the Revenue whether your property qualifies. If you move, give the Commissioner a new billing address, because bills go to the last address on record.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants or unpaid taxes
sections.html:
College-town sellers tend to land in one of a few spots.

  • A rental near campus with a lease that ends mid-year.
  • An inherited house with family members living out of state.
  • A house with deferred repairs and a roof or furnace near the end of its life.
  • Taxes that went unpaid after a death or a move.

Tenants make a standard listing harder: showings need advance notice and some buyers want vacant possession. Many cash buyers will take the house with the tenant still inside, bound by the lease. Hand over a copy early so the offer accounts for it. Rental registration and short-term rental rules differ from place to place, so ask the city.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
No buyer's loan means the calendar depends on the title work and on how quickly you can produce documents. You describe the house, the buyer takes a look, and an offer arrives in writing. Say yes and a title or settlement company searches for liens, then sets up the closing.

Keep the deed handy, plus any bill that touches the closing, such as the December 5 or June 5 installment. If the owner has died, bring proof of who may sign. You set the closing day, within what the title search permits.

Before accepting, do the arithmetic. A listing means repairs, agent fees and months of taxes, utilities and insurance while the house sits. With two tax dates a year, those carrying costs are easy to overlook, so count at least one installment if the house might be on the market through a bill date. Compare that net figure to the cash offer.

sections.h2: Paperwork for a rental or inherited house
sections.html:
Owners who live somewhere else often sell without walking through the place again, so a short checklist helps.

  • The deed, the latest tax bill and any loan payoff letter.
  • For a rental: the lease, rent records and deposit details.
  • For an inherited house: the court papers naming who may sign for the estate.
  • Ages of the roof, furnace and water heater, because an inspector will ask.
  • A note on repairs you already know about, big or small.

With these in hand you can settle questions in one phone call, and nobody has to hold up the closing while a missing signature turns up.

sections.h2: Questions to put to any buyer
sections.html:
Our offer or anyone else's, a few questions are worth raising. Who covers title and settlement charges? Could the price shift after the walk-through? What if the closing day has to move? Insist on a written offer, and compare the settlement statement with it line by line before you sign.

When a tenant lives in the house, find out how the buyer plans to treat the lease and the security deposit. Hearing a clear answer today beats arguing with a tenant later.

faqs.a: It is the county seat but a separate, independent city, and the city itself bills its own taxes.

faqs.q: What is the Harrisonburg real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's rate is $1.01 per $100 of assessed value for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. City Council votes on it every April.

faqs.q: When are Harrisonburg property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 5 covers July through December, and June 5 covers January through June. When a date falls on a weekend or holiday, payment is due the next business day.

faqs.q: What happens if I pay a Harrisonburg tax bill late?
faqs.a: The city adds a 10 percent penalty, with a $10 minimum. Interest of 10 percent a year then begins January 1 for the first half or July 1 for the second.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Harrisonburg house with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer purchasing as-is can take the house with tenants in place, but the existing lease still applies, so share it when you ask for an offer.
